purpose: Source-backed starter renderers for choosing concrete shipped SF5 components and smart custom-elements from Tailwind-like HTML snippets.

renderers.title: SF5 button
manualChecks: Confirm native submit behavior before replacing a submit button with a custom element.
Preserve disabled, loading, aria-label, icon, and destructive/action semantics.
Use native button markup when the target runtime does not hydrate smart custom elements.

renderers.title: SF5 dropdown
renderers.starterMarkup: <sf-dropdown size="1" type="outlined" mode="single" label="Label" placeholder="Select value" text="Value"></sf-dropdown>
manualChecks: Preserve original option values, selected state, disabled state, and form field name.
Confirm whether filtering/search inside the dropdown is required.

renderers.title: SF5 input
manualChecks: Preserve name, type, value, required, autocomplete, aria attributes, and validation hooks.
Use native input fallback when browser autofill or password manager behavior is critical.
Confirm masks, hints, errors, icons, and country-code behavior separately.

renderers.title: SF5 pagination
manualChecks: Use this renderer only for the source-backed SF5 full pagination contract; do not auto-promote compact previous/next-only pagers.
Check the rendered result against the real ui-play source example, not against a handcrafted approximation.
Confirm current page, total pages, URL policy, and AJAX vs full reload behavior.
Preserve accessible labels for numeric, page-size, and last-page controls.
Check mobile wrapping, disabled edge states, and whether top/bottom sections should be enabled.

renderers.title: SF5 modal
renderers.starterMarkup: <sf-modal id="modal-example" size="1" type="default" scheme="primary" title="Modal title" text="Modal content"></sf-modal>
manualChecks: Preserve trigger wiring, close controls, focus trap expectations, escape behavior, and overlay policy.
Confirm static content vs remote src mode.
Check accessibility labels and initial open/hidden state.
